correctness.rationale: Affine normalization preserves independent uniform edge fractions and the area ratio. In cyclic order the sampled shoelace sum on the normalized quadrilateral is the ratio, since the host area is 1/2. Independently checked the moments by conditioning: set c=p+q-1, d=p-q, S=X+Z, D=X-Z, with X,Y,Z,T the independent centered Uniform[-1,1] side coordinates. The shoelace expression gives F=4(R-1/2)=C+(W+H)T+(W-H)Y with C=-dD, W=(S+cD)/2, H=dS/2+c. The joint law of (S,D) allows either sign to be flipped separately. Thus E[F]=0; in the conditional cube only C^3+2C(W^2+H^2) survives averaging over T,Y, and both terms average to zero. In the conditional fifth power, C^5 and (20/3)C^3(W^2+H^2) likewise average to zero. The remaining term is (16/3)C(W^4+W^2H^2+H^4); the only contribution after taking the (S,D) expectation is -(8/3)c^2d^2 E[S^2D^2], with E[S^2D^2]=2/5-2/9=8/45. Dividing by 4^5 gives the stated negative fifth moment. If d=0, flipping T,Y reverses F; if c=0, flipping X,Z reverses F. These transformations preserve the joint law. Off those lines the nonzero fifth moment excludes reflection symmetry. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; the conditional-moment calculation supplies an independent exact check. Scope excludes degenerate hosts, pooled boundary sampling, and claims about a density everywhere.

value.rationale: This solves a natural finite-distribution question on the full affine shape family: area complementation in law singles out exactly hosts with parallel opposite sides, even though usual skewness vanishes for every host. The fifth moment provides a sharp exact obstruction and the involutions explain why full symmetry, not merely a moment cancellation, holds on the two lines. The result neither assumes nor proves Euclidean reflection symmetry of the host.
